events.title: Nylon is first produced
events.description: At DuPont's Experimental Station in Wilmington, Delaware, chemist Wallace Carothers first produced nylon, the polymer that became the world's first fully synthetic fiber.
events.significance: Nylon changed the textile industry. It led to a wide range of synthetic materials, from stockings to parachutes to everyday plastics.

events.title: The February 28 Incident begins in Taiwan
events.description: Protests in Taipei over the government's Tobacco Monopoly Bureau turned into an island-wide uprising. The Kuomintang-led Nationalist government then suppressed it violently, and thousands of civilians were killed.
events.significance: The event shaped Taiwan's political history for decades. Today February 28 is Peace Memorial Day, when the nation remembers the victims.

events.title: Watson and Crick announce the structure of DNA
events.description: Cambridge scientists James Watson and Francis Crick determined that DNA has a double-helix structure. They announced the discovery on this day.
events.significance: The double helix explained how genetic information is stored and copied. It launched the era of modern molecular biology and genetics.

events.title: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme is assassinated
events.description: Olof Palme was shot dead on a Stockholm street as he walked home from a cinema. More than 130 people have confessed over the years, but the murder has never been officially solved.
events.significance: The killing shocked a country that thought of itself as peaceful and open. It remains one of Europe's best-known unsolved political crimes.

events.title: Pope Benedict XVI resigns
events.description: Benedict XVI, born Joseph Ratzinger, stepped down as head of the Catholic Church. He was the first pope to resign in almost 600 years, since 1415.
events.significance: The resignation broke a centuries-old precedent. It paved the way for the election of Pope Francis and changed how people think about the papacy.
